name: Chat input
purpose: Where the user asks GOV.UK Chat a question, pinned below the conversation: a field that grows as they type, a send button once there's a question, and a menu of things to do with the chat, such as clearing it.

origin.notes: ChatActionView and its DynamicTextEditor: a capsule of fills.surfaceChatAction, its corners rounded 25pt, 48pt tall for one line, with Ask a question... in text.chatTextArea. While it's empty, ChatMenuView's button is beside it. Once there's a question, the menu goes, and a 36pt send button in text.buttonSecondary, with SF's arrow.up, grows in at its corner. From 250 characters, it says how many are left, and over 300 how many too many, in red, and the question can't be sent. The Android app's ChatInput is the same, its corners rounded 24dp, with Material's vertical more icon for its menu.

action.description: Where the form goes when the question is sent, such as the page with its answer. Without one, it goes to the page it's on.

method.description: How the form is sent. get puts the question in the address of the page it goes to.

name.description: The field's name, which the question is sent as.

value.description: A question already typed, to show the field as the user is typing.

placeholder.description: Shown in the field while it's empty.

label.description: The field's name for screen readers. Without one, it's the placeholder.

inputs.content: The menu's items, <govuk-app-menu-button-item> elements, top to bottom, as the app has them: Clear chat, destructive, with the delete icon, then Privacy notice, About and Give feedback. Without any, there's no menu.

events.name: input
events.description: From the field, as the user types.

events.name: submit
events.description: From the form, when the user presses the send button. The question is its field's value.

events.name: click
events.description: From the menu's button, and from its items, when they're pressed.

rules: Put it in the screen's footer, with slot="footer", so it's pinned below the conversation, and above the tab bar, if the screen has one.
Use one on every GOV.UK Chat screen, including a new chat and while an answer is being generated, as the app does.
Give it the app's menu: Clear chat, Privacy notice, About and Give feedback.
Give it an action to take the user to the next page of a prototype when they send a question, such as its answer.

references.description: Empty, with the menu button beside it, in light mode
A warning above the field, in light mode, drawn without its capsule, as the test draws it
An error above the field, in dark mode

examples.name: Empty, with its menu
examples.html:
<govuk-app-chat-input>
  <govuk-app-menu-button-item name="clear-chat" destructive icon="delete">Clear chat</govuk-app-menu-button-item>
  <govuk-app-menu-button-item name="privacy">Privacy notice</govuk-app-menu-button-item>
  <govuk-app-menu-button-item name="about">About</govuk-app-menu-button-item>
  <govuk-app-menu-button-item name="feedback">Give feedback</govuk-app-menu-button-item>
</govuk-app-chat-input>

examples.name: With a question
examples.html:
<govuk-app-chat-input value="How do I renew my passport?">
  <govuk-app-menu-button-item name="clear-chat" destructive icon="delete">Clear chat</govuk-app-menu-button-item>
  <govuk-app-menu-button-item name="privacy">Privacy notice</govuk-app-menu-button-item>
  <govuk-app-menu-button-item name="about">About</govuk-app-menu-button-item>
  <govuk-app-menu-button-item name="feedback">Give feedback</govuk-app-menu-button-item>
</govuk-app-chat-input>
